title: Ever had something arrive broken? Juniper Market uses Refund Relay, a refund agent that puts it right through PayPal, in seconds.
rule1: First, a peek behind the counter. The owner tells their refund agent what it may settle on its own, in plain English.
rule2: The agent reads the rules back, with a daily limit, so there are no surprises.
rule3: One click, and the agent is on duty.
store1: Now, me. I'm shopping for mugs and a vase.
paid: Paid in a couple of taps.
report: Everything I buy gets its own “Report a problem” link.
chip1: One mug arrived chipped. I say what happened, and add a photo.
refunded: A few seconds later, my twenty dollars is back in PayPal. Nobody at the shop lifted a finger.
case: In the shop's Refund Relay console, the case shows what happened: my photo was checked, and the agent refunded me under the owner's rule.
asst0: Next time, I didn't even open the site. I just asked my own assistant.
asst1: It reported the broken mug through the shop's own connector, and the refund agent paid me back through PayPal.
asst2: Agent to agent. No forms, no waiting on hold.
vase1: A cracked vase isn't in the owner's rules, so the agent leaves it for them, and says why.
vase2: The owner gets a hand: the shop's own repair kits, and something else in stock that would make up for it.
vase3: One click sends me the choices.
vase4: I can always take a full refund…
wrong1: This photo shows a printed mug, but the shop sold a plain white one.
wrong2: So nothing is paid out. The agent holds back, and the owner asks for a photo of the label.
log: The owner sees everything the agent did, and why, and can switch it off any time.
inbox: Small damage, settled in seconds. Everything else reaches the owner, already checked.
end: Refund Relay. Turn a broken order into the next sale.
